name: my5G-RANTester
what_it_is: A Go-based tool that emulates the control and data planes of UE (user equipment) and gNB (5G base station) for studying 3GPP Release 15+ standards and stress testing 5G cores. It can simulate a large number of UEs registering against a real or emulated 5G core network without implementing a wireless channel.
components: gNB emulator (NGAP control interface + GTP-U data interface)
protocols: NGAP (NG Application Protocol, control plane gNB↔AMF over SCTP port 38412)
NAS / NAS-5GS (Non-Access Stratum, 5G mobility and session management)
GTP-U (GPRS Tunnelling Protocol – User plane, UDP port 2152)
measurement: Registration latency per UE in milliseconds (ue-latency-interval command)
AMF response count over a timed interval (amf-load-loop command)
AMF availability check over a timed interval (amf-availability command)
Healthcheck: presence of uetun1 tunnel interface after UE attach
configuration: gnodeb.controlif.ip / port — gNB NGAP bind address (default 127.0.0.1:9487)
gnodeb.dataif.ip / port — gNB GTP-U bind address (default 127.0.0.1:2152)
gnodeb.plmnlist — MCC, MNC, TAC, gNB ID
ue.msin / key / opc / amf / sqn / dnn — SIM and subscription credentials
Docker env vars: NGAP_LOCAL_ADDR, NGAP_REMOTE_ADDR, GTPU_LOCAL_ADDR, MCC, MNC, TAC, GNBID, SST_GNB, SST_UE, SD, MSIN, OPC, KEY, AMF, SQN, DNN, NUM_UE
fault_injection: No explicit fault-injection primitives; amf-availability command can detect AMF downtime by repeatedly attempting registration over a configurable interval
modes: ue — attach a single UE with static config
gnb — attach a single gNB with static config
amf-load-loop -n <rps> -t <seconds> — send N registration requests per second for T seconds
ue-latency-interval -n <N> — measure average registration latency over N requests
amf-availability -t <seconds> — continuously probe AMF availability for T seconds
constraints: Wireless channel is NOT implemented — radio layer is entirely bypassed; tool tests core network only
Requires NET_ADMIN capability (or privileged mode) to create uetun1 tunnel interfaces for user-plane traffic
Designed to connect to an external 5G core (e.g., free5GC, Open5GS); docker-compose reuses an existing 'docker_privnet' network rather than spinning up its own core
Single gNB ID per run — all UEs in load-test share the same gNB instance
Built on free5GC libraries; SIM credentials (KEY, OPC) must match those provisioned in the target core's subscriber database
docker_services: my5grantester — single service; image my5grantester:latest; attaches to external network docker_privnet at 10.100.200.200; requires NET_ADMIN + privileged; entrypoint sleeps until commands are exec'd manually
notable_absences: No built-in 5G core — must be provided externally (e.g., free5GC, Open5GS)
No radio / air-interface simulation (no RF channel, no handover, no interference)
No HTTP/2 or SBI (Service Based Interface) — only RAN-to-core NGAP/NAS/GTP-U
No PDU session data-plane traffic generation beyond tunnel creation (no iperf-style throughput test)
No PCAP capture integration built in
No multi-gNB load distribution across separate gNB instances
